passage:
Monday. Mahima leaned over the desk. "Tell me what Tanvi told you about her brother and I'll be your best friend forever." Deepak's stomach dipped. He had eaten lunch alone all week. "No," he said, and looked at his pencil box.

Wednesday. She was waiting by the water cooler. "Last chance. Otherwise nobody sits with you." Deepak's hands felt cold, but he said, "That's not being friends. I'm not telling," and walked to the library.

Friday. Mahima blocked the corridor again, whispering the same demand. This time Deepak went straight to the class teacher and told everything, even the part where he had almost said yes. The teacher thanked him and said they would talk to Mahima.

qa.q: What did Mahima want Deepak to tell her?
qa.a: She wanted to know what Tanvi told him about her brother.

qa.q: Why might Deepak have felt tempted on Monday even though he said no?
qa.a: He had eaten lunch alone all week, so the offer of a best friend was tempting, though he still said no.

qa.q: What did Deepak's choice on Friday accomplish?
qa.a: Telling the class teacher moved the pressure from him to an adult who could talk to Mahima, so he did not have to handle it alone.

qa.q: How might Tanvi feel if she learned what happened?
qa.a: She might feel relieved and grateful that her secret stayed safe, though she may not know how close it came.

grounding: A classmate offers friendship only in exchange for someone's secret; the child says no, walks away and finally tells an adult when she keeps pressing.

Monday. Alka leaned over. "If you tell me what Meher said about her parents, I'll let you sit with us at lunch."
Zainab's stomach dropped. She had been eating alone all week. "No," she said.
Wednesday. Alka tried again. "Come on. Just one little secret. Then we're friends." Zainab looked at her tiffin. That's not friendship, she thought. That's a trade.
"No, Alka. That's Meher's secret."
Friday. Alka kept pushing, now in front of others. Zainab walked away and went to Ms Iyer. Ms Iyer listened and said, "You did right. I'll talk to Alka." She did, before the last bell.

qa.q: What did Alka offer Zainab for Meher's secret?
qa.a: "I'll let you sit with us at lunch."

qa.q: How did Zainab feel when Alka first made the offer?
qa.a: Her stomach dropped; she felt lonely and tempted, since she had been eating alone all week.

qa.q: What did Zainab do that was wise?
qa.a: She said no, recognised it was a trade not friendship, walked away and told Ms Iyer when Alka kept pushing.

qa.q: How might Meher feel if she knew Zainab protected her secret?
qa.a: Meher would feel grateful and safe that Zainab didn't give in.

grounding: A classmate offers friendship in return for another girl's secret; the protagonist says no, walks away and tells an adult when pressure continues.

passage:
"Arohi, your Jasleen Bua once had to choose between a friend and doing what was right. When I was ten, a popular girl, Harleen, said, 'Tell me what Gurdeep told you about her brother, and you can be in our group.'
Oh, I wanted to be in that group. They had the best games.
But I thought: if Harleen wants secrets to be friends, she'll sell mine too. So I said, 'No. It's Gurdeep's.' And I walked off.
Harleen kept asking all week. In the end I told our teacher, who spoke to her. It wasn't easy. But Gurdeep and I are still friends today."

qa.q: What did Harleen want young Jasleen to tell?
qa.a: What Gurdeep had told her about her brother.

qa.q: How did young Jasleen feel about Harleen's offer?
qa.a: She felt tempted and lonely for the group, because they had the best games.

qa.q: What turning point helped young Jasleen?
qa.a: Realising Harleen would sell her secrets too, so she said no, walked off and later told the teacher.

qa.q: How might Gurdeep have felt if the secret had come out?
qa.a: Gurdeep would likely have felt betrayed and hurt.

grounding: An aunt recalls a classmate offering friendship for someone's secret; she said no, walked away and told a teacher when the pressure continued.
